items.title: Use `nvml` to detect CUDA driver version
items.reason: Canonical discussion of the same detection request. Comments cover static musl builds that cannot dlopen, working cuda-compat containers without NVML or nvidia-smi, Python subprocess costs, WSL, and compute-capability discovery through driver interfaces or hardware mappings.

items.title: Directly ask the NVIDIA kernel driver what version it is
items.reason: Prototype linked from astral-sh/uv#14664 adds a /dev/nvidiactl ioctl probe before nvidia-smi, targeting speed and installations without the CLI. Its patch detects the kernel driver version only; compute-capability queries remain discussion, and it does not resolve cuda-compat user-mode version selection.

items.title: Implement a vendored nvidia variant provider
items.reason: Merged on October 22, 2026, before this report, and introduced the relevant wheel-variant provider. Source still queries nvidia-smi for CUDA user-mode version and compute capability. Review explicitly discusses missing nvidia-smi, static-build dlopen constraints, and deferred CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES filtering; this is implementation context, not a completed fix.

items.title: `--torch-backend=auto` ignores CUDA compute capability when installing `torch` for GTX 1080 Ti
items.reason: Demonstrates why compute capability matters: automatic selection installs cu128 wheels that cannot run on an sm_61 GPU, while cu126 works. Maintainer discussion considers NVML. It concerns compatibility-aware Torch wheel selection, whereas this report focuses on obtaining capabilities reliably.

items.title: `--torch-backend=auto` fails on systems with multiple GPUs and without `/proc/driver/nvidia/version`
items.reason: Historical WSL/multi-GPU failure in the same nvidia-smi fallback: repeated driver-version lines caused a version parse error. Fixed by astral-sh/uv#15460. This report requests broader detection and does not show that parsing bug recurring.

items.title: Respect multi-GPU outputs in nvidia-smi
items.reason: Merged November 2, 2025, fixing astral-sh/uv#14647; current source parses the first driver-version line. The author explicitly omitted NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES masking. It fixes multiline parsing, not CLI-independent detection or GPU-visibility handling.

related.search_scope: Searched astral-sh/uv open and closed issues and open, closed, and merged PRs with authenticated gh. Separate literal searches covered nvidia-smi, compute capability, cuda-compat, /sys/module/nvidia/version, libcuda.so.1, nvcuda.dll, sm_arch, CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES, and both NV_VARIANT_PROVIDER_FORCE overrides. Conceptual searches covered NVML, CUDA/dlopen/static builds, GPU detection, forward compatibility, WSL, torch-backend auto, and wheel variants. Checked closed detection reports and historical fixes; followed comments, review threads, and timeline references to astral-sh/uv#14743, astral-sh/uv#15460, and astral-sh/uv#22690. PR keyword searches returned no hits even for known matching PRs, so supplemented them with a 1,000-PR all-state listing and direct reads of linked PRs. Ruled out astral-sh/uv#17236 as a duplicate: uv pip detection worked, and the remaining problem was unsupported torch-backend configuration in uv sync. Broader wheel-variant discussions astral-sh/uv#16522 and astral-sh/uv#22043 were less specific.

type_reason: Open astral-sh/uv#14664 already tracks the same unresolved request, including the static-linking, missing userspace tools, cuda-compat, and compute-capability constraints. The new platform-specific proposals extend that discussion and can be centralized there. No return of the separately fixed multiline-output bug is established; astral-sh/uv#22690 predates this report and does not solve the requested detection improvements.
summary: Duplicate of astral-sh/uv#14664, with an open ioctl prototype in astral-sh/uv#14743. Merged astral-sh/uv#22690 provides the current wheel-variant implementation; astral-sh/uv#14742 documents the compute-capability selection problem. The historical multi-GPU parsing failure was fixed separately.
draft_response: This detection work is already tracked in astral-sh/uv#14664, including static builds, cuda-compat environments without NVML or nvidia-smi, and compute-capability discovery. The provider added in astral-sh/uv#22690 still uses nvidia-smi for CUDA-version and compute-capability detection; astral-sh/uv#14743 explores direct kernel-driver queries. Please add your platform-specific findings to astral-sh/uv#14664 so we can keep the API and support-scope discussion together.
